summary: Charles proves birational boundedness for holomorphic symplectic varieties, constructs Zarhin-type fourfolds from K3 surfaces over any field, and deduces the Tate conjecture for K3 surfaces over finite fields of characteristic at least 5, and of any characteristic when the Picard number is at least 2. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement and cited input is an item, and every missing item is routed exactly once. Lemma 4.5 is restated and proved after a finite extension (E8). Twenty-one findings are recorded, including the unverified nonsuperspecial hypothesis for the partners (E21). Supplier proofs are deferred. Not formalised.

items.name: K3 surfaces
items.statement: A K3 surface over k is a smooth projective geometrically integral surface X with ω_X≃O_X and H¹(X,O_X)=0; geometric base change is denoted X_kbar. Polarizations are ample line bundles, not assumed primitive.
items.note: No K3-surface, Mukai-moduli, IHS or Beauville–Bogomolov implementation was found in the full pinned source trees. Source-extracted target, not a claim of a complete proof-leaf audit; see prerequisite register and gaps. API: base change; polarization transport; canonical bundle and H¹ access. Tests: (1) Base change of a K3 remains K3; (2) A smooth quartic surface has trivial canonical bundle; (3) An abelian surface is excluded by H¹(O)≠0.

items.name: Nikulin primitive embedding criterion in signature (2,1)
items.statement: For an even positive definite rank-two lattice S and n>0, a primitive embedding S→Λ₂n exists iff there are subgroups H_S⊂A_S,H_q⊂A_Λ₂n and an isometry γ of their restricted full-norm forms for which δ=(q_S⊕−q_Λ₂n)|Γ_γ^⊥/Γ_γ is isometric to the cyclic form on Z/(2t) with generator norm 1/(2t), for some t>0. This is an existence criterion. The general classification includes a chosen complement K and discriminant identification γ_K, then quotients by the stated isometries; it is not a bijection of raw embeddings with tuples.
items.note: G5 initial-primitivity and embedding-versus-sublattice conventions have now been resolved. Nikulin primary text pp128–130 read through the publisher web PDF; full local PDF acquisition and deeper genus-classification proofs remain outstanding.

items.name: Congruence transport from a primitive initial embedding
items.statement: Given d>0, an even positive definite rank-two lattice S and a primitive embedding S→Λ₂d, there are N>0 and a,b≠0 such that every m>0 satisfying m≡1 mod N, gcd(m,ab)=1 and a,b invertible squares modulo m admits a primitive embedding S→Λ₂md. The initial primitivity is a necessary correction to the printed statement: arbitrary rank-two sublattices do not suffice.
items.note: The counterexample in nonprimitive-obstruction disproves the literal all-sublattices version already at m=1. Saturation of S does not repair that literal assertion. The actual Zarhin construction uses the explicit primitive input of item41.

items.name: Cyclic gluing-quotient transport
items.statement: Under m≡1 mod 4dt and |A_Λ| and the finite coprimality exclusions in the proof, Id⊕m maps the old discriminant data into A_Λ⊕A₂md. The new Γ^⊥/Γ is cyclic of order 2tm; its generator has full norm 1/(2t)+y₀²(m−1)/(2md).

items.name: Generator rescaling congruence
items.statement: With the preceding gluing data, a generator of norm 1/(2tm) is obtained from λ≡1 mod 4dt and λ²ty₀²+d≡0 mod m. The assumptions that −d,t are invertible squares modulo m solve this congruence by CRT and ensure λ is prime to 2tm.

The span S=Zv+Zw is primitive and positive definite, with Gram matrix [[2,1],[1,2dk²]], v²=2,v·w=1,l·v=0 and l²=2(4dk²−1)>0. If a specified integer n is odd, choose k a positive multiple of |n|; then gcd(l²,n)=1. After primitive congruence transport, the pairing v·w=1 supplies the Mukai gcd condition, and an allowed hyperbolic isometry makes the rank positive.

items.name: Frobenius-invariant lattice discriminant bounds
items.statement: Fix rank r>0, an even weight w≥0 and q. For a nondegenerate O-lattice M, O the integers of a finite unramified extension of Qℓ, with integral characteristic polynomial for φ, all roots Weil q-integers of weight w, semisimple q^(w/2)-eigenvalue and (φx,φy)=q^w(x,y), the q^(w/2)-eigenlattice discriminant valuation is at most vℓ(disc M) for ℓ>C(r,w,q), and at most C′(r,w,q)+vℓ(disc M) for all ℓ. This controls valuations, not a common rational square class.

items.statement: For K3 surfaces over finite fields, the geometric Frobenius action on H²_et(X_kbar,Qℓ) is semisimple in the Deligne result used by LMS; its integral characteristic polynomial and weights are independent of ℓ.

items.name: Nonzero transcendental invariants from infinite Brauer
items.statement: For X over finite k, failure of Tate (infinite Br(X)) gives nonzero T(X,Zℓ) for each ℓ≠p. For ℓ∤disc NS and sufficiently large ℓ, its pairing is unimodular and the Kummer map T⊗Qℓ/Zℓ onto B-field Brauer classes is an isomorphism.

items.name: Norm-one vectors in the transcendental lattice (corrected Lemma 4.5)
items.statement: Let X be a K3 surface over a finite field k with NS(X_k̄) = NS(X) and Br(X) infinite. Assume Frobenius acts semisimply on the eigenvalue-1 part of H²(X_k̄, Q_ℓ(1)) (item 111) and that −1 is not a Frobenius eigenvalue on it. The second condition holds after a finite extension of k, which keeps Br(X) infinite. Let g be the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius on the complement of the invariants, and put c = −g(1)g(−1)·disc NS(X) ∈ Q^×. Let x_1, …, x_r be −1 and the primes dividing the numerator or denominator of c. Then for every sufficiently large ℓ such that each x_i is a square modulo ℓ, there is α ∈ T(X, Z_ℓ) with α² = 1. The printed lemma omits the eigenvalue condition and −1 (E8).
items.note: Restated by Claude Code (cc-442dc5, 23 September 2026) with the rational-discriminant repair of E8, and routed. It gives the printed form of the lemma after the finite extension, with −1 among the p_i. The checkpoint's split-prime substitute (items 114 and simultaneous-k3-norm) is kept. Proposed target; no Lean declaration is claimed.

items.name: Safe norm-representation substitute after quadratic extension
items.statement: In the stated p≥5 scope of LMS §3.5, after the quadratic finite-field extension k′/k and assuming Br(X_k′) infinite, any rational d is represented in T(X_k′,Zℓ) for infinitely many ℓ. For d≠0 choose large odd ℓ splitting the field generated by Frobenius eigenvalues and √−1, √d, √disc NS; exclude denominators. Rank ≥2 uses finite-field forms and Hensel, rank one the reciprocal-eigenspace decomposition. Extending this replacement to p=2,3 requires an explicit hypothesis audit.

items.statement: A nondegenerate quadratic form of dimension at least two over Fℓ, ℓ odd, represents every nonzero element. This is the finite-field input to the separate Hensel lift, not a theorem for a degenerate form.

items.statement: For q>0 and a∈(Z/qZ)×, infinitely many rational primes p satisfy p mod q=a.

items.name: Simultaneous quadratic-residue primes
items.statement: For finitely many integers x₁,…,x_s, infinitely many primes ℓ make all x_i squares modulo ℓ. Factoring them and imposing ℓ≡1 modulo 8 and each relevant odd prime gives the result by quadratic reciprocity and Dirichlet; finitely many excluded primes may be removed.

items.name: Simultaneous splitting and congruence prime choice
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension E/Q, a positive integer N and any finite set S of rational primes, infinitely many l∉S split completely in E and satisfy l≡1modN. Apply the identity-class infinitude theorem to E*Q(ζ_N). This imposes only the identity congruence; an arbitrary residue class may be incompatible with splitting.

items.name: Hypotheses of Proposition 3.17 for the twisted partners
items.statement:
In the proof of Theorem 1.3 (characteristic ≥ 5, X nonsuperspecial, D ample of square 2d):
(a) For each n, one of H_n^{±1} is ample on X_n. This follows from a deformation of (X, D) over a DVR whose generic fibre has Picard rank one, carrying the ℓ-power Brauer class α_n and v_n, and from item 128 applied to the relative moduli space.
(b) Proposition 3.17 then applies to (X_n, H_n^{±1}), of degree 2dℓ^{2n}, for every n with ℓ^{2n} ≡ 1 mod N and X_n nonsuperspecial.
The paper verifies neither that the X_n are nonsuperspecial nor that infinitely many admissible n have X_n nonsuperspecial (E21).
items.note: Restated by Claude Code (cc-442dc5, 23 September 2026) and routed. Part (a) is the paper's sketch completed by item 128. The family's construction is a supplier step (G4). Part (b)'s nonsuperspecial hypothesis is the paper's gap E21. Proposed target; no Lean declaration is claimed.

items.name: Special-fiber ampleness from a rank-one projective deformation
items.statement: Let Y→Spec R be a smooth projective family of surfaces with geometrically integral fibers over a DVR, H a line bundle, and Pic(Y_η)⊗Q of rank one generated by H_η with positive square. A relative ample A and the injectivity Pic(Y)→Pic(Y_η) imply a positive rational multiple of H or H^−1 equals A in Pic(Y)⊗Q, hence that choice is ample on the special fiber. Generic ampleness alone, without the rank-one/proportionality argument, is insufficient.

items.statement: For complex abelian varieties A,B, integral Hodge morphisms on H¹ arise contravariantly from algebraic homomorphisms B→A; rationalizing yields the rational Hom comparison. In particular an integral Hodge endomorphism of H¹(A) comes from End(A).

items.name: Prime-to-n orthogonal norm by one explicit choice
items.statement: For d>0 and any odd integer n, choose k>0 divisible by |n|. Then l²=2(4dk²−1)≡−2 modn, so gcd(l²,n)=1. This provides the exact initial lattice needed by the prime-to-n part of Theorem2.10.
items.note: Continuation by Codex, codex-c83e7a. Proposed proof/API decomposition, not a new formalization.

items.name: Two quadratic polynomials over a finite odd field
items.statement: For a finite integral domain F of odd cardinality and polynomials f,g∈F[T] of degree exactly two, there exist x,y with f(x)+g(y)=0. In particular a*x²+b*y²=t has a solution for all nonzero a,b and all t∈F.

items.name: Nondegenerate quadratic forms diagonalize with unit weights
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic different from two, a quadratic form with separating associated bilinear form is equivalent to a weighted sum of squares whose weights are units.

items.name: Existing plain discriminant and its orthogonal-sum law
items.statement: TauCeti.RegularFormClass.discr is the plain Gram-determinant square class. The discriminant of an orthogonal sum is the product of its two discriminants, written as addition in the library’s additive SquareClassGroup. This is not the signed discriminant.

items.name: Identity Artin class and complete splitting
items.statement: For a prime of a number field unramified in a finite Galois extension, its Artin class is the identity exactly when the number of primes above it equals the extension degree. Over Q this means e=f=1 at every prime above the rational prime; the residue-field map from F_l is bijective.

items.name: Arithmetic Frobenius on roots of unity
items.statement: For a number field K, extension field F, an m-th root of unity ζ∈F, a height-one prime q of the integers of K avoiding m, an ideal Q above q and an arithmetic Frobenius σ at Q, σ(ζ)=ζ^(Norm q). For primitive ζ, the cyclotomic character of σ is Norm q modulo m. In particular an identity Frobenius over Q forces l≡1 mod m.

items.name: A completely split prime gives a Q_l embedding
items.statement: Let E/Q be a finite Galois number field and l a rational prime splitting completely in E. For each place w above l, the canonical completion E_w is Q_l as a Q_l-algebra. Composition with E→E_w gives a Q-embedding E→Q_l. Consequently a polynomial splitting in E splits in Q_l, and every rational radicand whose square root belongs to E is a square in Q_l.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Reciprocal eigenspaces form a hyperbolic block
items.statement: Let V carry a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form over a field F of characteristic different from two, and let φ be a diagonalizable isometry with all eigenvalues in F. If λ≠±1, then V_λ and V_(λ⁻¹) are totally isotropic, pair perfectly with one another, and have equal dimension r. Their sum has Gram matrix [[0,I_r],[I_r,0]] in dual bases and plain discriminant (−1)^r modulo squares.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Discriminant of the squared-isometry fixed space
items.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, W=ker(φ²−1)=V_1⊕V_(−1) is nondegenerate. If n=dim V−dim W, then n is even and disc(W)=(−1)^(n/2)disc(V) in F×/(F×)². In particular W has square discriminant if both −1 and disc(V) are squares in F.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Unimodular sublattices split integrally
items.statement: Let M be a finite free Z_l-module with an integral symmetric pairing, and P⊂M a finite free submodule whose restricted Gram determinant is a unit. Then M=P⊕P⊥ integrally. If M is unimodular, so is P⊥; its determinant is disc(M)/disc(P) modulo unit squares.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Unimodular odd-adic lattices represent units in rank at least two
items.statement: Let l be odd and let M be a finite free Z_l-module of rank at least two with a unimodular symmetric pairing B. For every t∈Z_l× there exists a primitive v∈M with B(v,v)=t. No representation claim for every nonunit t is made.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: A square discriminant solves the rank-one norm equation
items.statement: For a rank-one unimodular Z_l-lattice with generator e of norm u∈Z_l×, if u and the target t∈Z_l× are squares in Q_l, then the lattice has a primitive vector of norm t. For l odd, being a square in Q_l is equivalent to the unit’s reduction being a square in F_l.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: The geometric K3 pairing has determinant square class minus one
items.statement: For a K3 surface X over an algebraically closed field and l different from its characteristic, H²_et(X,Z_l(1)) is free of rank22 with a perfect cup-product pairing; its plain determinant has square class −1 in Q_l×/(Q_l×)². This is a statement about the full geometric pairing, not its Frobenius invariants.
items.locator: Huybrechts author draft, Chapter1 §3, pp16–18, Proposition3.5 and Remark3.7; LMS Lemma3.5.2 p302

items.name: Norm selection from split orthogonal compatible systems
items.statement: For each sufficiently large odd prime l let M_l be a unimodular Z_l-lattice with semisimple isometry φ_l whose characteristic polynomial is one fixed P∈Q[T], and suppose disc(M_l⊗Q_l) is one fixed rational square class δ. Put N_l=M_l∩ker(φ_l²−1), assume N_l unimodular, and let A_l⊂N_l be isometric to A⊗Z_l for a fixed nondegenerate integral lattice A. Suppose T_l=A_l⊥∩N_l has positive rank. Fix t∈Q×. If l avoids the numerators/denominators of t,δ and disc A and the splitting field E of P together with √−1,√δ,√(disc A),√t embeds into Q_l, then T_l contains a primitive vector of norm t.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Residue squares lift to every prime power
items.statement: Let l be odd, a∈Z prime to l, and a a nonzero square modulo l. Then a is a square modulo l^m for every m≥1. If also l≡1 mod N with N≥1, then l^(2n)≡1 mod N for every n≥1.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: The common splitting field for the K3 prime choice
items.statement: After first choosing k0/k with geometric NS defined over k0, let k1/k0 be quadratic. Fix D∈NS(X_k1) with D²≠0 and, when using Proposition3.17, choose its constants N≥1,a,b∈the nonzero integers over k1. Put t=−D², s=disc NS(X_k1), and let E/Q be the finite Galois compositum of the splitting field of the Frobenius polynomial over k0, Q(i), Q(√t), Q(√s), Q(√2), Q(√a), Q(√b), and Q(ζ_N). Choose one finite exceptional set containing2,p, the prime divisors of N,t,s,a,b and the invariant-pairing exceptions for k1. Every sufficiently large prime splitting E satisfies all required rational square and congruence conditions simultaneously.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

api.name: Charles16.primeChoiceData.compositum
api.statement: Construct the finite Galois compositum inside a fixed algebraic closure of Q from the Frobenius polynomial and the listed rational radicands and cyclotomic field.

api.name: Charles16.primeChoiceData.goodPrimes
api.statement: A completely split prime outside the explicit finite set supplies a Q_l embedding, every listed unit square root and l≡1 mod N.

api.name: Charles16.primeChoiceData.enlarge
api.statement: Adjoining finitely many additional radicands or replacing N by a multiple produces a stronger prime condition with infinitely many solutions by the same identity-class supplier.

uses.how: Provides the same primes for norm representation and every n-dependent polarization congruence.

items.name: Rational divisor Tate descends along a finite extension
items.statement: Let X be smooth projective over a finite field k, k1/k finite of degree e, and l≠char k. If the rational divisor cycle map is surjective onto the Frobenius invariants over k1, then it is surjective over k. This implication concerns Q_l coefficients; it does not assert integral surjectivity. Consequently failure of rational Tate persists after any finite field extension.
items.locator: Charles Theorems1.3–1.4 finite-extension reductions; direct trace argument with cycle-class suppliers

items.name: The composed K3 prime choice in characteristic at least five
items.statement: Let X/k be K3 over a finite field of characteristic p≥5 and suppose its rational divisor Tate conjecture fails. After a finite extension k0/k defining geometric NS and the quadratic extension k1/k0, fix D∈NS(X_k1) with D²≠0 and constants N≥1,a,b∈the nonzero integers. There are infinitely many odd l, outside any further finite set, with l≠p, l∤N*a*b*D²*disc NS, l≡1modN, 2,a,b squares modulo every l^m, and a primitive γ∈T(X_k1,Z_l) satisfying γ²=−D². Thus for every n≥1 the same l makes m=l^(2n) satisfy Proposition3.17’s congruence and square conditions. The other moduli/polarization hypotheses of that proposition are separate.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Unit norm detects primitive classes and exact quotient order
items.statement: Let M be finite free over Z_l with integral symmetric pairing, P⊂M a unimodular sublattice, and γ∈P⊥ with unit norm. Then γ is primitive in P⊥ and its image in M/P is not divisible by l. The image of γ/l^n in (M/P)⊗_(Z_l)(Q_l/Z_l) has exact order l^n. Identifying this quotient with a Brauer subgroup requires the separate Kummer comparison.
items.locator: LMS §3.5, published p302; Charles §4.2 pp520–522; proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Determinant of an isometry space without eigenvalues ±1
items.statement: Let (V, b) be a finite-dimensional nondegenerate symmetric bilinear space over a field of characteristic not 2, and F an isometry of V whose characteristic polynomial g satisfies g(1)g(−1) ≠ 0. Then dim V is even and det b ≡ g(1)g(−1) modulo nonzero squares.
items.locator: Charles Lemma 4.5 repair (E8); proof supplied in this continuation

items.name: Low-degree Hodge–de Rham degeneration for admissible triples
items.statement: In the setup of Definition 3.8 (k perfect of characteristic p > 3), the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence of M_0 satisfies E_1^{p,q} = E_∞^{p,q} for p + q = 1, 2, and h^{2,0}(M_0) = h^{0,2}(M_0) = 1.
